To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the virtual is no more or less than a reflection of the human, embodied reality.
the Internet is not a virtual world, and that virtual environments are not virtual worlds.

(a) cyberspace is a virtual reality; (b) cyberspace has a profound effect on human beings; and (c) this effect is more profound for the challenge it offers to identity construction than it is for its emancipator function.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ways in which virtual leisure technologies are being constructed and consumed in the contemporary social world and how they are implicated in the construction of the human subject.
the question of what virtual leisure means for the human condition and the human experience of reality.
how virtual leisure is used in contemporary society, and how it is used to reflect upon the human condition.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the significance of cybervirtual reality is not that it is virtual, but that it is a virtual reality that is so close to human reality that its virtualness can no longer be ignored.
cyberspace is not the ‘technotopia of postmodernity’, nor is it a world of infinite freedom.
virtual reality is a technology that has the potential to change leisure and culture.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cyberspace is a virtual reality which is a sophisticated extension of human reality, and which challenges the very basis of human identity.
the virtual world is not a world of infinite possibilities but rather a world that is limited to the human imagination.
cyberspace, like other leisure technologies, has the potential for both good and bad outcomes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Internet is not a virtual reality, but it is a real reality.
virtual environments are no more or no different than any other environment.
the Internet is an important tool in the fight for gender equality, but that it is not a tool that can be used to solve all problems.
